label: text
text: GOVERNMENT'S REPLY

label: text
text: At the meeting of the Legislative Council this afternoon, the following questions were asked in the name of Hon. Mr. P. H. Holyook:

label: text
text: |Questions:—

label: text
text: (1) What steps are being taken to improve the Fire Brigade fire fighting appliances and water pressure—in the mains of the Colony?

label: text
text: (2) Will the Government appoint a Committee of Enquiry into these matters?

label: text
text: Answers:—

label: text
text: The Government has decided to appoint a Committee to consider and report on measures for improving the fire fighting organisation in the Colony.

text: Falling from a wall ten feet high, Chinese working for the Naval Ordinance Department was injured and sent to the Government Civil Hospital yesterday.

label: paragraph_title
text: REPULSE BAY.

label: text
text: REQUEST FOR COMMITTEE OR ENQUIRY

label: text
text: GOVERNMENT'S ATTITUDE.

label: text
text: Iton. Sir. H. E. Pollock, K.C. asked the following questions at this afternoon's meeting of the legislative Council:—

label: text
text: Questions:

label: text
text: (1) Will the Government appoint a Committee for the purpose of considering and reporting the this Council on the following questions in connection with Repulse Bay, namely:—

label: text
text: (a) The feasibility of providing better bathing accommodation.

label: text
text: (b) The feasibility of enlarging the area of the beach which can be bathed from by the removal of rocks from "the western end of the Bay.

label: text
text: (c) The provision of the proper sanitary conveniences for those resorting to Repulse Bay.

label: text
text: (d) The regular removed by scavenging coolies of rubbish and refuse and tins from the houses and beach.

label: text
text: (e) The regular inspection by a Sanitary Inspector of the septic tanks and drainage and other outlets, for the purpose of ensuring that the same are working effectively and without danger to the public health.

label: text
text: (f) The cutting and keeping cut; and the removal of all rubbish and refuse and tins from, the long grass and other undergrowth below the Hotel Garage, and in such other places as are recommended by the above.Committee.

label: text
text: (g) Generally, the making of such recommendations as may tend to improve the bathing and public health conditions at Repulse Bay and to check the breeding of flies and mosquitoes.

label: text
text: (2) Will the Government also empower the above Committee to consider and report upon the feasibility of inaugurating a new public bathing beach in the neighbourhood of Stanley?

label: text
text: The reply to these questions is not yet ready.

label: text
text: Answers:

label: text
text: Sir Henry Pollock asked that expediency would be exercised in regard to a reply in view of the near approach of the bathing season and H.E. the Governoror gave an assurance.

label: paragraph_title
text: TEN DAYS?

label: paragraph_title
text: LENGTHY WING ON BANK

label: text
text: The initial proceedings in the alleged conspiracy on the Wing On Bank case havings occupied a day and a hall, Mr. E. C. Jenkins concluded this opening to press this morning and the first part of the evidence was called. The whole case is expected to last ten days or a fortnight.

label: text
text: In his concluding research, M. F. C. Jenkins referred to "somehow found" on the premises of Au Kim-hui referring to the raising of money for the purpose of putting it in to the Wing On Bank and to letters written by Au Kim-hui admitting what he in person had attended with the deposit book on April 25.

label: text
text: Referring to the two counts under which Au Kin-lui was charged with perjury, Mr. Jenkin said that the swprn statement of Au in connection with an attempt to make the Wing, On Bank pay by means of a civil action that the Wing, On Bank was indebted to him for the amount of $50,000 was wholly untrue and Au knew it to be false because he knew that the book under which he claimed it was forged and that the money had already been withdrawn.

label: text
text: Au had made another sworn statement in which he said that he had in his possession a deposit book issued by the defendants, the only inference being that it was a genuine one. This also was false, said Mr. Jenkins, because Au knew that the book was not the original deposit book but that book altered, in that it had a false label. If you tamper with a document, said Mr. Jenkins, by removing part of it, it is not the same document but a forgery.

label: text
text: The statement made at the magis- iracy by Chan Sam was also the subject of reference by counsel. In this, Chan had stated that he had been informed by the two-third soners and the third who had abseonded of "the ramp" they intended to work on the Wing On Company by means of the forgeries.

label: text
text: This statement, claimed counsel, was strengthened by the fact that Chan Sam was the man whom it had been decided should look after the affairs of the alleged conspirators in their civil action with the Wong On Bank whilst Au Kim-lui was absent in Peking on one occasion. Mr. Hugh Jones, of Wilkinson and Grist, would speak at a later stage of an interview which took place in their offices between the three parties prior to Au Kim-lui's departure at which it was arranged that Chan Sam should take over in his absence.

label: text
text: The other two parties: the present second prisoner and the man who had absconded, did not wish to be publicly associated, said counsel, with a case which in the event of trouble they would easily have been identified with if they had done so.

label: text
text: The only evidence called this morning was that of Detective Sub-Inspector Fallon who made the arrest.

label: text
text: At yesterday afternoon's hearing of the case, a reading lamp, together with a cardboard screen, were placed in front of the jury by Mr. Jenkin so that when the various deposit books and other exhibits in the case were held in front of the light, counsel had the opportunity of demonstrating his various points.

label: text
text: The alleged forgery of the chop and labels were dealt with and counsel pointed out what he alleged were differences in parts of the chops alleged to have been forged and the others stamped on the books by the Wing On Company.

text: KARAKHAN TO GO.

label: text
text: CHANG TSO-LINS GRAVE WARNING.

label: text
text: DRAMATIC EXPOSURE

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service).

label: text
text: Shanghai, April 22.

label: text
text: A Mukden (correspondent publishes a report that Chang Tso-lin has requested the Soviet Consul-General here to warn the Moscow Government of the necessity of replacing M. Karakhan, the Soviet Ambassador, Peking, on the ground that "since his arrival in China he has employed bribery to cause student riots and assisted Feng Yu-hsiang with arms in order to create internal strife in China, which actions constituted a misuse of his Ambassadorial position and a violation of international usages."

label: text
text: The Consul-General was further informed that when Peking was occupied by the allied troops M. Karakhan no longer would be considered entitled to the protection of international law.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINA'S WARS.

label: text
text: PROTECTION OF FOREIGNERS IN PEKING.

label: text
text: ELIMINATING BOLSHEVISM.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Peking, April 22.

label: text
text:
The Superintendent of Police visited the Senior Minister to-day and gave an assurance that, although Tuan Chijul's Government had suddenly been dissolved, the Police authorities would take all necessary measures to protect foreign life and property.
It is reported from Hankow that Wu Pei-fu at a conference of his lieutenants, expressed the opinion that Bolshevist influence in China should be eliminated and that the Tariff Conference should proceed in compliance with the people's will.

label: paragraph_title
text: W. W. Yen As Premier.

label: text
text: The present arrangements are that Tsao Kun will be restored to the Presidency, after which he will issue a mandate rescinding his resignation on the grounds that it was due to force majeure.

label: text
text: This procedure will reinstate as Premier W. W. Yen, who thereupon will fill the vacancies in the former Cabinet.

label: text
text: Tsao Kun will then hand over to W. W. Yen as head of the governing Cabinet.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE FOUND WITH DAGGERS.

label: text
text:
Defending two Chinese young men charged at the Central Magistracy this morning with unlawful possession of three daggers. Mr. C. A. S. Russ tendered a plea of guilty and pointed out that the daggers (or knives) were in common use in Java for peeling fruit and opening coconuts. He said the men were labourers returning from Java and passing through here on their way to Foochow. He asked for a small penalty as there had been no unlawful intent.
To a question by the Magistrate (Mr. R. E. Lindsell), Sergeant Flaherty said the police had no reason to doubt that the men were merely passing through the Colony. Each of the accused was fined

label: text
text: Each of the accused was fined $50, or four weeks' hard labour, and the weapons were confiscated.
